title: Fruquintinib (Fruzaqla) monotherapy
context_label: Metastatic colorectal cancer after standard therapies and trifluridine/tipiracil or regorafenib
purpose: Fruquintinib is a targeted capsule treatment to help control bowel cancer that has spread after previous treatments. The team checks which treatments you have received, whether they remain suitable, and your priorities.
schedule_summary: Take the prescribed fruquintinib dose once daily on Days 1–21, then take no fruquintinib on Days 22–28. Take it at about the same time each day, with or without food. Repeat only when your team authorises the next cycle.
scope_note: The team confirms the full treatment history, including chemotherapy, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR treatment where applicable, and progression or intolerance on trifluridine/tipiracil or regorafenib.
schedule_label: 21 days of capsules, then seven days without capsules
indication_text: NCCP 00890a: metastatic colorectal cancer after available standard therapies, with progression on or intolerance to trifluridine/tipiracil or regorafenib.
phases_note: No fixed final cycle. Continue only while benefit and tolerability justify treatment.
timeline_note: The calendar shows capsule days and rest days. Symptoms are not confined to a particular week.
safety_note: Use your oncology unit’s urgent contact plan throughout the cycle, including tablet-free days. Symptoms can need attention before the next blood test or appointment.
teachback: Can you show the 21 tablet days and seven rest days, explain the meal and missed-dose instructions, identify the early liver and blood-pressure checks, and say whom you will call if unwell?
consent_support: Discuss the previously treated colorectal setting, benefit and uncertainty, alternatives, blood-pressure and urine monitoring, hand-foot effects, fatigue, mouth/bowel/appetite effects, serious bleeding, clotting, bowel perforation and neurological risks, wound healing, pregnancy precautions, medicine interactions and the option to reconsider.
urgent_extra: Get urgent help for severe or persistent tummy pain, black or bloody stools, coughing or vomiting blood, new severe headache, confusion, seizure, visual change, chest pain, sudden breathlessness or very little urine. Report fever, sudden illness, painful hands/feet and new bleeding promptly.

agents.name: Fruquintinib
agents.explanation: Fruquintinib blocks VEGF receptor signals that help tumours form blood vessels. Reducing these signals can slow cancer growth. Blood vessels in healthy tissues are also affected, which helps explain blood-pressure, bleeding, protein-in-urine and wound-healing risks.
agents.watch: Report painful hands/feet, bowel changes, bleeding or neurological symptoms; attend blood-pressure, urine and blood checks even if well.
risks: High blood pressure, including severe hypertension
Protein in urine and kidney complications
Bleeding, bowel perforation, clotting and impaired wound healing
Thyroid changes, liver-test abnormalities, diarrhoea, fatigue, appetite/weight loss and mouth soreness
Rare serious neurological or blood-vessel complications

passport_visit_note: Record the prescribed dose, treatment days, rest days, blood-pressure readings and tests. A diary entry is not permission to restart after a hold.
anatomy: Fatigue and thyroid changes can affect daily life. Severe headache, confusion, seizure or visual change needs emergency help.
Mouth soreness, voice change and poor appetite can affect eating. Report difficulty drinking or weight loss.
Blood pressure may rise without symptoms. Keep scheduled checks. Chest pain, collapse or severe breathlessness needs emergency care.
New bleeding, easy bruising, fever or sudden illness needs prompt advice. Heavy bleeding needs emergency help.
Liver tests can change before symptoms occur. Report yellow eyes or skin, dark urine or persistent abdominal pain.
Diarrhoea can cause dehydration. Severe persistent pain, black stools or blood in stools needs urgent help.
Pain, redness, swelling or blisters can affect walking or using your hands. Report early and follow the skin-care plan.
Protein in urine may have no early symptoms. Attend urine checks and report swelling or much less urine.
anatomy_note: Selected effects; blood-count and skin markers are schematic. This is not a prediction or a complete side-effect list.
administration_text: The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily, but follow your own label. Swallow capsules whole with water, with or without food; do not chew, dissolve or open them. Tell the team before starting if swallowing capsules is difficult.

phases.detail: Take the prescribed fruquintinib dose once daily on Days 1–21, then take no fruquintinib on Days 22–28. Take it at about the same time each day, with or without food. Repeat only when your team authorises the next cycle.

timeline.label: Fruquintinib capsules
timeline.text: Once daily, with or without food

timeline.label: Capsule-free week
timeline.text: No fruquintinib; review recovery and next prescription

timeline.label: Symptoms, BP and tests

day_groups.title: Start with a clear calendar
day_groups.body: Take the prescribed daily dose with or without food. Keep blood-pressure appointments and check hands and feet.
day_groups.action: Confirm the first tests, urine checks and skin-care instructions.

day_groups.title: Continue capsules and monitoring
day_groups.body: Symptoms may develop over time. Report painful hands/feet, bowel changes, poor appetite, bleeding or fatigue.
day_groups.action: Blood pressure is checked weekly during the first month. Do not wait until the rest week to report problems.

day_groups.title: Capsule-free week
day_groups.body: Take no fruquintinib. Symptoms may persist. The team may delay the next cycle or prescribe a lower dose.
day_groups.action: Complete planned checks and confirm the next dose and start date.

support.title: Skin care
support.text: Use the unit’s skin-care plan and report redness, pain, swelling or blisters early. The team may prescribe creams or change treatment. Do not wait until walking or everyday hand use is difficult.

support.title: Sickness and bowels
support.text: This oral medicine has minimal-to-low emetogenic potential. Routine premedication is not usually needed; agree any anti-sickness and diarrhoea medicines with the team. Persistent vomiting, diarrhoea, poor intake or reduced urine needs prompt advice.

support.title: Blood pressure and medication review
support.text: Take prescribed blood-pressure medicines and keep monitoring visits. Tell the team about anticoagulants and every prescription, over-the-counter and herbal medicine.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Use highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least two weeks after the last dose if you could become pregnant. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least two weeks afterwards.

monitoring_schedule.note: NCCP specifies regular blood/urine/thyroid tests but no universal frequency for each. Ask your team to write the dates. Scans and tumour markers are individualised.

monitoring_summary: Baseline and regular blood count, kidney/liver profile, thyroid function and urine protein. Blood pressure must be controlled before starting, then checked weekly for the first month and monthly thereafter, or more often if needed. For warfarin, INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle. Scans and markers follow the consultant plan.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment and rest days
chronology_notes.text: Take the prescribed fruquintinib dose once daily on Days 1–21, then take no fruquintinib on Days 22–28. Take it at about the same time each day, with or without food. Repeat only when your team authorises the next cycle.

chronology_notes.title: Monitoring even when well
chronology_notes.text: Baseline and regular blood count, kidney/liver profile, thyroid function and urine protein. Blood pressure must be controlled before starting, then checked weekly for the first month and monthly thereafter, or more often if needed. For warfarin, INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle. Scans and markers follow the consultant plan.

chronology_notes.title: Dose changes
chronology_notes.text: Only your prescribing team changes the dose or authorises a restart. A rest week does not guarantee recovery.

sections.title: Prescription and calendar
sections.text: Take the prescribed fruquintinib dose once daily on Days 1–21, then take no fruquintinib on Days 22–28. Take it at about the same time each day, with or without food. Repeat only when your team authorises the next cycle.

sections.title: Taking capsules
sections.text: The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily, but follow your own label. Swallow capsules whole with water, with or without food; do not chew, dissolve or open them. Tell the team before starting if swallowing capsules is difficult.

sections.title: Missed or vomited dose
sections.text: If a dose is less than 12 hours late, take it and then follow the usual schedule. If more than 12 hours late, skip it and take the next dose at the normal time. At exactly 12 hours, or if unsure, ask your pharmacist or team. Do not take a replacement capsule after vomiting; take the next dose at the usual time.

sections.title: Tests and visits
sections.text: Baseline and regular blood count, kidney/liver profile, thyroid function and urine protein. Blood pressure must be controlled before starting, then checked weekly for the first month and monthly thereafter, or more often if needed. For warfarin, INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle. Scans and markers follow the consultant plan.

sections.title: Storage
sections.text: Keep the original bottle tightly closed to protect from moisture and out of children’s sight and reach. No special temperature conditions are required. Follow the expiry date and ask the pharmacist how to return unused capsules; do not put them into household waste or wastewater.

sections.title: Treatment changes
sections.text: Your team must confirm dose changes and restarts. Bring the capsule pack, current calendar and medicine list to review.

evidence.title: Evidence in previously treated colorectal cancer
evidence.intro: FRESCO-2 compared fruquintinib plus best supportive care with placebo plus best supportive care after previous metastatic colorectal treatments.
evidence.population: Previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer; participants had received or could not tolerate trifluridine/tipiracil, regorafenib, or both.
evidence.interpretation: Median overall survival was 7.4 months with fruquintinib and 4.8 months with placebo. These group medians are not a prediction of one person’s lifespan or a guaranteed extra 2.6 months. The team should discuss the balance of benefit and side effects for you.
evidence.limitations: The result applies to the trial population and treatment setting. It does not mean all patients benefit or that earlier-line treatments are interchangeable.

chapters.title: Why this treatment may be offered
chapters.intro: Confirm the treatment history and personal goals.

items.title: Previously treated bowel cancer
items.text: Fruquintinib is a targeted capsule treatment to help control bowel cancer that has spread after previous treatments. The team checks which treatments you have received, whether they remain suitable, and your priorities. The team confirms the full treatment history, including chemotherapy, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR treatment where applicable, and progression or intolerance on trifluridine/tipiracil or regorafenib.

items.title: Evidence and uncertainty
items.text: Median overall survival was 7.4 months with fruquintinib and 4.8 months with placebo. These group medians are not a prediction of one person’s lifespan or a guaranteed extra 2.6 months. The team should discuss the balance of benefit and side effects for you.

items.title: Treatment duration
items.text: There is no fixed total number of cycles. Continue while benefit and tolerability justify it; the team reviews symptoms, scans, tests and your preferences.

chapters.title: How fruquintinib works
chapters.intro: It affects signals involved in blood-vessel growth.

items.title: VEGF receptor signals
items.text: Fruquintinib blocks VEGF receptor signals that help tumours form blood vessels. Reducing these signals can slow cancer growth. Blood vessels in healthy tissues are also affected, which helps explain blood-pressure, bleeding, protein-in-urine and wound-healing risks.

items.title: Safety checks
items.text: Blood-pressure and urine-protein changes can develop without symptoms. Tests and early symptom reporting help the team decide whether treatment can safely continue.

chapters.title: Your capsule and rest-day plan
chapters.intro: Use your own prescription and calendar.

items.title: Days 1–21 and Days 22–28
items.text: Take the prescribed fruquintinib dose once daily on Days 1–21, then take no fruquintinib on Days 22–28. Take it at about the same time each day, with or without food. Repeat only when your team authorises the next cycle.

items.title: Swallow whole, with or without food
items.text: The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily, but follow your own label. Swallow capsules whole with water, with or without food; do not chew, dissolve or open them. Tell the team before starting if swallowing capsules is difficult.

items.title: Missed or vomited dose
items.text: If a dose is less than 12 hours late, take it and then follow the usual schedule. If more than 12 hours late, skip it and take the next dose at the normal time. At exactly 12 hours, or if unsure, ask your pharmacist or team. Do not take a replacement capsule after vomiting; take the next dose at the usual time.

items.title: If too much is taken
items.text: Contact your doctor immediately if you take more than prescribed. You may need medical attention; take the pack and treatment calendar with you.

chapters.title: Checks and follow-up
chapters.intro: Feeling well does not replace testing.

items.title: Before and during treatment
items.text: Baseline and regular blood count, kidney/liver profile, thyroid function and urine protein. Blood pressure must be controlled before starting, then checked weekly for the first month and monthly thereafter, or more often if needed. For warfarin, INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle. Scans and markers follow the consultant plan.

items.title: If a test is abnormal
items.text: The team may arrange extra blood or urine tests, treat hypertension, pause capsules, reduce the dose or stop treatment. Do not change the dose yourself.

items.title: Scans and tumour markers
items.text: The consultant decides the imaging and marker schedule for your situation. This regimen does not mandate a fixed CT or CEA interval.

items.title: After a pause or stopping
items.text: Ask who follows persistent symptoms and abnormal tests, and when the next review is due. Do not restart without clear instructions.

chapters.title: Skin, mouth, eating and energy
chapters.intro: Early support can help preserve daily activities.

items.title: Hands and feet
items.text: Use the unit’s skin-care plan and report redness, pain, swelling or blisters early. The team may prescribe creams or change treatment. Do not wait until walking or everyday hand use is difficult.

items.title: Bowels, fluids and sickness
items.text: This oral medicine has minimal-to-low emetogenic potential. Routine premedication is not usually needed; agree any anti-sickness and diarrhoea medicines with the team. Persistent vomiting, diarrhoea, poor intake or reduced urine needs prompt advice.

items.title: Mouth and appetite
items.text: Report mouth soreness, voice changes, poor appetite or weight loss. Ask for mouth care and nutritional support. Drink as advised for your health.

items.title: Fatigue and thyroid
items.text: New marked fatigue, feeling unusually cold, weight or skin changes may need thyroid assessment. Balance activity with rest and report symptoms affecting usual activities.

items.title: Driving
items.text: Do not drive or use machinery if tiredness or other symptoms affect concentration or reactions.

chapters.title: Symptoms needing urgent help
chapters.intro: A rare effect may still need immediate care.

items.title: Bleeding and bowel problems
items.text: Seek urgent help for black or bloody stools, blood in urine, coughing/vomiting blood, severe or persistent abdominal pain. Heavy bleeding or collapse needs emergency care.

items.title: Neurological, heart or vascular symptoms
items.text: Severe headache with confusion, seizure or visual changes, chest pain, severe breathlessness, sudden weakness or sudden severe chest/back/abdominal pain requires emergency help.

items.title: Kidneys, skin and infection
items.text: Report much less urine or swelling, painful hands/feet, fever, shivering or suddenly feeling unwell. Symptoms may need assessment even during the capsule-free week.

chapters.title: Other medicines, wounds and procedures
chapters.intro: Tell every treating team you take fruquintinib.

items.title: Medication review
items.text: Tell the pharmacist about anticoagulants, antibiotics, infection treatments, seizure medicines, herbal remedies and supplements. Rifampicin and other strong enzyme inducers can affect fruquintinib exposure. Ask before starting or stopping anything.

items.title: Wound healing and surgery
items.text: Report unhealed wounds and planned surgery. Product information recommends withholding fruquintinib for at least two weeks before surgery and not restarting for at least two weeks afterwards and until adequate wound healing. Your oncology and surgical teams must agree the exact plan; do not stop or restart it yourself.

items.title: Allergies
items.text: Tell the pharmacist about medicine or colouring-agent allergies. Capsule colours differ by strength and contain colouring agents that can cause allergic reactions.

chapters.title: Pregnancy precautions and safe storage
chapters.intro: Keep the medicine in its labelled packaging.

items.title: Pregnancy and feeding
items.text: Use highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least two weeks after the last dose if you could become pregnant. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least two weeks afterwards.

items.title: Storage
items.text: Keep the original bottle tightly closed to protect from moisture and out of children’s sight and reach. No special temperature conditions are required. Follow the expiry date and ask the pharmacist how to return unused capsules; do not put them into household waste or wastewater.

items.title: Your treatment record
items.text: Carry the wallet card and current medicine list. Record the prescribed dose, any holds, symptoms, BP and upcoming tests. Replace all example telephone numbers with your real oncology contacts before using the card.
